findings.title: All-used federated recovery codes are removed through the local credential API
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now prefers federated credentials, so when the final recovery code is used, removeStoredCredentialById may be called with a federated credential ID. This API removes only credentials stored in the Keycloak DB, not federated user-storage credentials. If the federated provider returns a CredentialModel without a local DB id, such as the included test provider does, the call can no-op or throw. As a result, the user can keep an all-used credential and may be repeatedly forced to reconfigure recovery codes, or login may fail instead of completing cleanly.

findings.title: Plaintext recovery codes are passed to user storage
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated recovery codes and passes them as the challengeResponse to user.credentialManager().updateCredential. The local Keycloak provider hashes recovery codes before persisting them, but user-storage providers receive the plaintext codes. The included test provider stores exactly this value in credentialData. A production user-storage provider following the same pattern would store usable recovery codes unhashed, exposing valid recovery credentials if the external user store is compromised. Consider passing only hashed values or explicitly enforcing hashing in the user-storage SPI contract.

findings.title: Recovery code form can throw NoSuchElementException for user-storage credentials
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns an Optional, but this code immediately calls get(). Since recovery codes can now be created in user storage, a provider that implements updateCredential/isValid for recovery codes but does not expose them through getFederatedCredentialsStream/getCredentials (where the default is empty) will cause getCredential to return empty and the login form to throw NoSuchElementException while rendering, instead of showing a proper challenge or error.

findings.title: Federated recovery credential test model loses the stored ID and does not consume codes
findings.body: getCredentials builds a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the raw stored codes but does not copy myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(), so the returned credential id is null. It also validates the raw code list without marking the entered code as used. This is the provider used to cover the new user-storage recovery path, so the test does not exercise final-code consumption or removal and hides the all-codes-used removal problem in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.
